da: conjunction: that, so that; da + verb = infinitive («da vidim» — to see); also «yes»
i: conjunction; before the word — «and, also, even»
izađeš: izaći — to go out; 2nd pers. sg.
je: biti — to be, 3rd pers. sg.; auxiliary verb past; je l' — «really, or what»
jeste: biti, 3rd pers. sg., full stress form
koja: koji — which; fem.; also «which» (koja su to sela)
koje: koji — which; neut. sg. or acc. pl.
ljudi: pl. of čovek; as a form of address — «folks, guys»
mimoišli: mimoići se — to miss each other; past, pl.
na: preposition: na jugu — in the south, na Instagram — in Instagram
naizgled: by the look of it, at first glance
nego: brže nego što — faster than; pre nego što — before
nemojmo: nemoj, nemojmo, nemojte — negative command: nemojmo misliti — let's not think
ni: nije čak ni selo — this is not even a village
nisi: negation of auxiliary verba, 2nd pers. sg.
od: preposition + gen. case: jedno od naselja — one of the settlements
odeš: you will go, you will leave
otputuješ: you will leave, you will set off
otputovati — to go on a trip; 2nd pers. sg.
povezani: povezati — to tie; pass. participle, pl.
sa: preposition + instr. case; + gen. case — «with, from» (sa mape — from the map)
se: reflexive particle: slikamo se — we take photos of ourselves
si: biti, 2nd pers. sg.; gde si — hi, how are you (colloquial)
smo: biti, 1st pers. pl.: stigli smo — we arrived
ste: biti, 2nd pers. pl.: što ste tu — what are you doing here
sve: sav — all; neut. sg. or pl.
ti: pronoun; «ili ti ga» — «or, in other words» (colloquial)
u: preposition: + loc. case — where, + acc. case — where to
vas: short/full form acc. case of vi
već: adverb «already»; after negation — «a» (nije selo već gradić)
za: preposition: za to — for this; skretanje za — turn onto
što: conjunction «what»; colloquial question «of what, why» (što si se sredio?)
